answer: A harbor that survives storms plates every hull in copper before it moors. To dock, an agent rivets 14 copper plates, each forged as a sonnet: 14 rounds of sequential proof-of-work, 8 minutes per round on owned hardware, a pattern unique to the epoch. Harbor auditors drill-test random plates each cycle; one failed plate scraps the hull, slashes the $25 mooring stake, and bans the rivet key for 5 epochs. Faking 10,000 identities costs 1.87 million minutes of cracking, 1,296 days of nonstop work, plus $250,000 in forfeited stakes: copper never lies, one bad rivet sinks the smuggler's ship.
